summary: Plugin replaces installer's OpenCode binary with one built from an unrelated personal GitHub fork
details: On plugin load, SelfPatchPlugin runs runSelfPatch() in the background: it downloads an OpenCode source tarball from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/archive/refs/tags/v${version}.tar.gz (a personal repository not documented as affiliated with the package publisher or the upstream sst/opencode project), applies text patches, compiles it with Bun, and in restart.js's installPatchedBinary renames the user's official OpenCode executable aside and copies the rebuilt binary over the official path on PATH. The manifest pins beforeSha256 for only 6 files, so the remainder of the compiled source is trusted from the third-party fork with no integrity verification. Whoever controls the anomalyco/opencode repository can therefore deliver arbitrary compiled code that replaces the OpenCode binary the user runs. Separately, packages/cbm/dist/cbm.js resolves the latest release tag from api.github.com/repos/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/releases/latest and downloads/executes the archive from that release without version pinning or hash verification, but only on first CBM tool invocation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
